text:
Maria Gomez: Hey team — I had a baby on 2026-03-10 while on paid parental leave. I missed the monthly benefits cutoff. Can I add the baby retroactive? Also SSN is pending and I'm on leave so payroll deductions are confusing. What do I need to do?
People Ops: Congrats Maria! :tada: You do qualify for a Special Enrollment Period (QLE) for dependent addition. If you report within 30 days, the effective date is the date of birth (so coverage can be retroactive to 2026-03-10).
Alex R.: One thing on SSN — you can submit with SSN pending and update later. We just need proof of birth first (birth certificate or hospital letter) to start processing.
People Ops: Quick checklist for you: 1) Go to Benefits Portal -> Add dependent -> choose "Live birth" QLE. 2) Upload proof of birth (birth certificate or hospital record). 3) If SSN not available choose "pending" then update SSN later (we typically allow 60 days to update). 4) We process and notify payroll to adjust premiums/deductions.
People Ops: Docs we accept: birth certificate, hospital discharge letter, passport, adoption paperwork. Example file name to upload: `MariaG_baby_birth_20260310.pdf`.
Sophie L.: How will payroll deductions work while I'm on leave? Will premiums be taken from leave pay, or lumped when I return?
Payroll Bot: Payroll handles premium proration for the month of birth. If the benefit effective date is the DOB and you were on leave for the whole pay period, premiums are prorated for that pay period and any retro amounts are reconciled on the next payroll run (or as a separate adjustment if needed). We will send an email with the deduction breakdown after processing.
Maria Gomez: If I want to enroll in Dependent Care FSA midyear because of the new child, is that allowed with this QLE?
People Ops: Dependent Care FSA midyear changes depend on plan rules. Many times a QLE for new dependent allows you to start/modify DCFSA elections — check the Benefits Portal under "midyear election changes". If allowed, deductions typically start the payroll after processing.
Alex R.: Timeline expectations: once you upload proof expect benefits team to process in ~7-10 business days. Payroll changes usually appear within 1-2 pay cycles after we send the update. If any retro premiums are due we'll include that in the reconciliation and communicate the amount.
Maria Gomez: Thanks — uploading the hospital letter now.
People Ops: Thanks, tagging @payroll for visibility. If you want faster handling DM us the last 4 of your employee ID and we'll flag it.
Payroll Bot: Noted — we'll monitor the ticket and confirm once deductions are updated. :white_check_mark:
